also: to lead someone by the nose

evidence: Plaut. Mil. 2.1.15: meretrīcēs eum labiīs ductant (Lewis & Short s.v. ductō: “to charm, allure”; s.v. labia: “to ridicule, make game of one”)
terms.comment: Literally “to lead someone by the lips”: in Plautus, of courtesans who lead a man on and make a fool of him. Traupman uses it for leading someone by the nose.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, cited by printed page; each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
